=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003): issues and recommended pushback
**Basis:** Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA, so the drafting points below need checking against the clause text.

## Executive view

The package is not balanced. Taken together, the Seller's positions would leave the Buyer with almost no remedy for the problems already identified. Three proposals combine to produce this:

1. **General disclosure** of the whole data room and public registers.
2. **A broad "Buyer knowledge" bar** that includes anything "discoverable."
3. **Caps, thresholds and time limits applying to all Claims**, including title, tax and indemnities.

Every known risk in this deal is in the data room: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the DD-006 incident and the Sandbar renewals. Under the Seller's drafting, each of these would be disclosed, known to the Buyer, and therefore not claimable. The rest would be capped at AUD 4.8m and lost after 18 months.

Meanwhile, the Disclosure Letter itself confirms that the main issues are **unresolved**:

- No Bluefen consent.
- Riverlark not repaid or discharged.
- No Ironquay assignment.
- Bonuses missing from the funds flow.
- The privacy incident is uninvestigated.

The Seller Update describes each of these as "addressed," "adequate" or "not material." **Rely on the Disclosure Letter, not the Seller Update's characterisations.**

Known risks should be dealt with through **completion deliverables, price mechanics and specific indemnities**, not through the warranty regime.

---

## Part A: Liability regime

### 1. General cap of 20% / AUD 4.8m (cl 12.1)
- **Issue:** On its own, 20% is within market range for general warranties, particularly with W&I insurance. It is acceptable only if fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities sit outside it. The Seller is proposing the opposite (see item 4).
- **Push back:**
  - Seek 30–50% if there is no W&I policy. Accept 20% only if W&I is in place, with a Seller retention or escrow.
  - Title, capacity, tax and specific indemnities should be capped at 100% of the price (AUD 24m).
  - Fraud should be uncapped.

### 2. De minimis AUD 25,000 and deductible basket AUD 250,000 (cl 12.2)
- **Issue:** The basket is about 1.04% of the price and works as a **deductible** ("only the excess is recoverable"). A Buyer-friendly position is a **tipping** basket, under which the full amount is recoverable once the threshold is crossed. The de minimis (about 0.1%) is within range, but it must allow related claims to be aggregated.
- **Push back:**
  - Tipping basket at about 0.5–1%.
  - Related or same-cause claims aggregate for both the de minimis and the basket.
  - Neither threshold applies to title, capacity, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, price adjustment or fraud.

### 3. Time limits and the "all Claims" catch-all (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Issue:** 18 months for general warranties is at the low end; 24 months gives a full audit cycle after Completion.
- **Main concern:** The sentence *"any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"* reverses the drafting default. It would silently extend caps and time bars to:
  - specific indemnities;
  - the tax covenant;
  - covenant breaches;
  - completion and price-adjustment claims; and
  - possibly leakage.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete the catch-all. Limitations should apply **only** to "Warranty Claims (other than Title, Capacity and Tax Warranties)."
  - Proposed time limits:
    - 24 months for general warranties.
    - 7 years for tax, or 3–6 months after the relevant ATO amendment period expires if that is later.
    - 7 years or the statutory limitation period for title and capacity.
    - Indemnity periods set per indemnity (see Part C).

### 4. Fundamental (title/capacity) warranties under the same cap and time limits
- **Issue:** This is not an "administrative simplification." The title warranty is the warranty that the Buyer is actually getting the asset it is paying AUD 24m for. Capping it at AUD 4.8m and 18 months is not market practice.
- **Push back:** Reject. Title and capacity should be capped at 100% of the price, with a 7-year (statutory) period, no de minimis or basket, and no disclosure against them.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Issue:** Read literally, this would cover fraud, wilful concealment, the specific indemnities, the tax covenant and claims for misleading or deceptive conduct.
  - Section 18 of the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contracted out of directly.
  - However, a broad non-reliance clause can undermine causation and reliance in practice.
- **Push back:**
  - Carve out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:
    - fraud, dishonesty and wilful misconduct or concealment by the Seller, its officers or advisers;
    - specific indemnities;
    - the tax covenant;
    - leakage and price adjustment; and
    - claims for specific performance or injunctive relief.
  - Non-reliance should be limited to statements outside the Warranties and the Disclosure Letter, and should not apply to fraud.

---

## Part B: Disclosure and knowledge

### 6. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Issue:** Under the Seller's draft, the Buyer is deemed to know everything in the data room and on public registers. This empties the warranties of content.
  - Clause 1.4 (no admission of breach, materiality or that any consent is required) adds to the problem, because it lets the Seller later argue that a disclosed issue was never a breach at all.
- **Push back:**
  - Only **specific** disclosures in the letter count.
  - Each disclosure must be **fair**: fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - Data room documents count only where a specific disclosure cross-references them.
  - Public register disclosure should be limited to searches of named registers (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia) on a stated date.
  - No disclosure against title, capacity or tax warranties, or against specific indemnities.
  - Indemnities should apply "notwithstanding any disclosure or Buyer knowledge."
  - Any disclosure update between signing and Completion should not cure a breach. Instead, it should give the Buyer a termination right.

### 7. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3)
- **Issue:** This is the most damaging clause in the package. It covers:
  - the knowledge of the Buyer **or its advisers**; and
  - anything **"discoverable"** from the data room or public records. That is a constructive-knowledge standard.
  
  In practice, every issue raised in due diligence is barred.
- **Push back:**
  - Preferred: a **pro-sandbagging** clause. The Buyer's rights are unaffected by any knowledge or investigation, except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Fallback: the bar applies only to **actual** knowledge of named individuals on the Buyer deal team, and only of the facts constituting the breach, at the date of the SPA. It should exclude advisers, imputed knowledge and anything "discoverable."

---

## Part C: Specific transaction risks

### 8. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3) — HIGH
- **Facts (DL 2):** Bluefen generates about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the total. Clause 11.2 is a change-control consent and clause 11.3 attaches conditions. **No consent has been given and there is no evidence the conditions are met.** The Seller Update's "addressed" is not accurate.
- **Issue:** The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and proposes that the condition is satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent. That written consent could be conditional, qualified, or impose obligations on the Buyer group under clause 11.3, such as guarantees, repricing or new terms.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **condition precedent** that Bluefen gives written consent that is unconditional, or subject only to conditions the Buyer approves in writing (acting reasonably), in a form the Buyer approves.
  - Any clause 11.3 conditions that fall on the Company must be satisfied before Completion.
  - The CP is waivable only by the Buyer.
  - The Seller must use **best or all reasonable endeavours**. The Buyer must not be required to incur cost or give guarantees.
  - Include a sunset date and a Buyer walk right.
  - Consider a warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received. Also consider a price adjustment or earn-out holdback if Bluefen terminates within, say, 12 months for change-of-control reasons.

### 9. Riverlark facility of about AUD 3.2m (cl 2 / 7) — HIGH
- **Facts (DL 3):** The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security has been provided. It contains change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.
- **Issue:** A "release to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. If the release does not arrive, Riverlark's security over the Company's assets (and possibly over the shares) survives, and Completion could itself trigger an event of default under clause 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion, require:
    - a **payout letter**; and
    - an executed **deed of release** under clause 9.2, covering all security, PPSR registrations and any guarantees from the Company.
  - Repayment should come out of the purchase price through the funds flow, paid directly to Riverlark, with PPSR discharges effected at Completion or held in escrow with the Buyer's lawyers.
  - The amount should be included in **Debt**, deducted from the price.
  - Confirm whether Riverlark holds a mortgage over the shares. If it does, this goes to title (see item 15).

### 10. DD-005 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 plus on-costs — HIGH (price leakage)
- **Facts (DL 5):** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. They are **not in the funds flow**, and the letter is silent on on-costs.
- **Issue:** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but does not fund them. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer effectively pays AUD 420,000 plus:
  - NSW payroll tax (currently about 5.45%, subject to threshold);
  - superannuation guarantee, if the bonuses are ordinary time earnings (to be confirmed);
  - PAYG withholding administration; and
  - workers' compensation premiums.
  
  The total exposure is roughly AUD 445k–500k.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses and all on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt**, deducted from the price. Alternatively, the Seller funds them at Completion through the funds flow, with payment processed through Company payroll.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall and any post-Completion bonus claims.
  - If the deal uses a locked box, these are **leakage**.
  - Confirm the documents give no Buyer-side retention obligation.

### 11. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1) — HIGH
- **Facts (DL 4):** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 outstanding. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Issue:** On those facts, the Company **may not own** the SOW3 IP. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment. It does not cover:
  - the Company not owning the IP;
  - third-party infringement claims;
  - the cost of re-engineering; or
  - lost revenue if the materials are used in core products.
- **Push back:**
  - Completion deliverables:
    - evidence of cleared payment, or payment out of the price through the funds flow; and
    - an executed **confirmatory assignment** from Ironquay of all SOW3 IP, including moral rights consents where relevant.
  - A specific IP indemnity covering all loss from any failure of title to the SOW3 materials. It should not be subject to the general cap, thresholds or disclosure, should last at least 6 years, and should be capped at the price or at an agreed figure supported by technical due diligence.
  - Have the technical team confirm how central the SOW3 materials are to the product.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6) — HIGH, unquantified
- **Facts (DL 6):** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may expose about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notifiability are unknown, and the investigation is still "preliminary."
- **Issue:** The Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material," but the disclosure itself establishes nothing either way.
  - Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment within 30 days. The letter is dated as at 22 September 2026 and today is 6 November 2026, so that window has very likely closed. A missed assessment or notification may be a separate contravention.
  - Exposure includes OAIC investigation, the increased civil penalties, the statutory privacy tort, customer contract claims (check whether Bluefen's contract has data or security clauses), and remediation costs.
- **Push back:**
  - Before signing or as a CP, require the full incident file: forensic report, access logs, the Company's NDB assessment and any notifications made.
  - Pre-Completion covenant that the Seller completes the investigation and makes any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer.
  - **Specific indemnity** for all loss arising from DD-006, including regulatory fines to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, third-party claims and remediation. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, last at least 3–4 years, and be backed by escrow.
  - Add an express warranty on compliance with the Privacy Act and data incidents. Confirm whether W&I insurers will exclude this as a known matter. They almost certainly will, which is why the indemnity matters.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals of AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts (DL 8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The letter says they should be "read together for timing/scope" and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Issue:** The Seller calls these "ordinary course," but the letter does not support that. Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three may have been done to stay under a materiality or Buyer-consent threshold in the conduct-of-business covenant or the material contracts definition. I can't confirm this without the full SPA thresholds. Please check.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain the contracts and confirm timing (before or after signing), term, termination rights, and whether they are related-party arrangements.
  - Add an aggregation rule: related contracts count together for all thresholds.
  - If entered after the relevant date without consent or outside the ordinary course, treat them as leakage or a Debt-like item, or require the Seller to procure termination.
  - Ensure any amount accrued or prepaid is properly reflected in working capital.

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Push back:** Reject.
  - **Tax:** A separate **tax indemnity / covenant** covering pre-Completion tax, capped at 100% of the price, running for the ATO amendment period plus a buffer. No disclosure against it and no de minimis or basket.
  - **IP:** IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement, assignments from employees and contractors, and open-source use. Put them at a higher cap, or treat key IP ownership as quasi-fundamental, given the Ironquay facts.

### 15. Title (DD-012)
- **Issue:** The Company's share register is the Seller's own record. DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Push back:**
  - Run ASIC company searches (members and share structure) and PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company. Also review constitution and shareholder documents for options, convertible notes, ESOP or pre-emption rights.
  - The title warranty must cover full legal and beneficial ownership free of all Encumbrances, with no options or rights to issue shares. Treat it as fundamental (see item 4).
  - Completion deliverables: share transfer, share certificates (or an indemnity for lost certificates), and releases of any share security, including possibly Riverlark's.

### 16. Lower-risk items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation only. Add a covenant that the Seller procures the notice is given on time, and confirm the lease contains no change-of-control termination right.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Confirm the clause contains no "deemed assignment on change of control" wording. If it does, treat it like Bluefen.

---

## Part D: Structural protections

- **Escrow or retention:** Hold back about 10–15% of the price (AUD 2.4m–3.6m) for 18–24 months to secure the specific indemnities. DD-006 is the priority because it is unquantified. Alternatively, require a creditworthy guarantee, because Harbourglass may distribute the proceeds.
- **W&I insurance:** Worth considering for general warranties. Known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar) will be excluded, so they must be covered by Seller indemnities or price.
- **Funds flow:** Reissue it to show Riverlark payout, the bonuses and on-costs, Ironquay payment (if made from the price) and Transaction Costs as deductions. Confirm whether the deal uses **completion accounts or a locked box**, because this affects how items 10 and 13 are treated.
- **Conduct of business:** Pre-Completion covenants should require Buyer consent for new or renewed contracts above a threshold, measured on an aggregated basis, for bonuses, and for any communications with regulators about DD-006.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) | 30–50%, or 20% only with W&I; cap applies to general warranties only | Medium |
| 2 | AUD 25k de minimis / AUD 250k deductible | Tipping basket, aggregation of related claims, carve-outs | Medium |
| 3 | 18 months; limitations apply to all Claims | 24 months general, 7 years tax/title; delete the catch-all | **High** |
| 4 | Title/capacity under general cap and time limits | 100% of price, 7 years, no thresholds or disclosure | **High** |
| 5 | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance cover all Claims | Carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, leakage, equitable relief | **High** |
| 6 | General disclosure of data room and registers | Specific and fair disclosure only; none against fundamentals or indemnities | **High** |
| 7 | Buyer/adviser knowledge, including "discoverable," bars claims | Pro-sandbagging; fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals | **High** |
| 8 | Bluefen: reasonable endeavours, any written consent suffices | CP for unconditional or Buyer-approved consent, best endeavours, walk right | **High** |
| 9 | Riverlark released after Completion | Payout letter and deed of release at Completion; repaid from price | **High** |
| 10 | AUD 420k bonuses outside funds flow | Debt/Transaction Cost deduction including on-costs, plus indemnity | **High** |
| 11 | Ironquay indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment plus confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad IP indemnity | **High** |
| 12 | DD-006 "not material" | Full incident file, NDB compliance, uncapped specific indemnity, escrow | **High** |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k is ordinary course | Diligence the contracts; aggregation rule; leakage/Debt treatment if improper | Medium |
| 14 | Tax/IP under general regime | Separate tax indemnity; enhanced IP warranties | **High** |
| 15 | Title evidenced by Company register | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; fundamental title warranty | Medium |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notice covenant; confirm no change-of-control trigger | Low |
| — | Security for claims | 10–15% escrow or guarantee; consider W&I | **High** |

**Recommended next steps:**
1. Obtain the full SPA text so these points can be checked against the actual clause wording and thresholds.
2. Request the outstanding diligence: the DD-006 incident file, Sandbar contracts, Riverlark payout figures and security documents, and Ironquay payment status.
3. Prepare a Buyer mark-up built on three principles:
   - specific, fair disclosure only;
   - pro-sandbagging; and
   - known risks dealt with through CPs, completion deliverables, price and specific indemnities.

This memo reviews negotiating positions. The NSW law, tax (payroll tax and super treatment of the bonuses) and Privacy Act points should be confirmed by the responsible practitioners before positions are finalised.

    - Indemnity periods set per indemnity (see Part C).

### 4. Fundamental (title/capacity) warranties under the same cap and time limits
- **Issue:** This is not an "administrative simplification." The title warranty is the warranty that the Buyer is actually getting the asset it is paying AUD 24m for. Capping it at AUD 4.8m and 18 months is not market practice.
- **Push back:** Reject. Title and capacity should be capped at 100% of the price, with a 7-year (statutory) period, no de minimis or basket, and no disclosure against them.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Issue:** Read literally, this would cover fraud, wilful concealment, the specific indemnities, the tax covenant and claims for misleading or deceptive conduct.
  - Section 18 of the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contracted out of directly.
  - However, a broad non-reliance clause can undermine causation and reliance in practice.
- **Push back:**
  - Carve out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:
    - fraud, dishonesty and wilful misconduct or concealment by the Seller, its officers or advisers;
    - specific indemnities;
    - the tax covenant;
    - leakage and price adjustment; and
    - claims for specific performance or injunctive relief.
  - Non-reliance should be limited to statements outside the Warranties and the Disclosure Letter, and should not apply to fraud.

---

## Part B: Disclosure and knowledge

### 6. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Issue:** Under the Seller's draft, the Buyer is deemed to know everything in the data room and on public registers. This empties the warranties of content.
  - Clause 1.4 (no admission of breach, materiality or that any consent is required) adds to the problem, because it lets the Seller later argue that a disclosed issue was never a breach at all.
- **Push back:**
  - Only **specific** disclosures in the letter count.
  - Each disclosure must be **fair**: fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - Data room documents count only where a specific disclosure cross-references them.
  - Public register disclosure should be limited to searches of named registers (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia) on a stated date.
  - No disclosure against title, capacity or tax warranties, or against specific indemnities.
  - Indemnities should apply "notwithstanding any disclosure or Buyer knowledge."
  - Any disclosure update between signing and Completion should not cure a breach. Instead, it should give the Buyer a termination right.

### 7. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3)
- **Issue:** This is the most damaging clause in the package. It covers:
  - the knowledge of the Buyer **or its advisers**; and
  - anything **"discoverable"** from the data room or public records. That is a constructive-knowledge standard.
  
  In practice, every issue raised in due diligence is barred.
- **Push back:**
  - Preferred: a **pro-sandbagging** clause. The Buyer's rights are unaffected by any knowledge or investigation, except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Fallback: the bar applies only to **actual** knowledge of named individuals on the Buyer deal team, and only of the facts constituting the breach, at the date of the SPA. It should exclude advisers, imputed knowledge and anything "discoverable."

## Part C: Specific transaction risks

### 8. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3) — HIGH
- **Facts (DL 2):** Bluefen generates about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the total. Clause 11.2 is a change-control consent and clause 11.3 attaches conditions. **No consent has been given and there is no evidence the conditions are met.** The Seller Update's "addressed" is not accurate.
- **Issue:** The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and proposes that the condition is satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent. That written consent could be conditional, qualified, or impose obligations on the Buyer group under clause 11.3, such as guarantees, repricing or new terms.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **condition precedent** that Bluefen gives written consent that is unconditional, or subject only to conditions the Buyer approves in writing (acting reasonably), in a form the Buyer approves.
  - Any clause 11.3 conditions that fall on the Company must be satisfied before Completion.
  - The CP is waivable only by the Buyer.
  - The Seller must use **best or all reasonable endeavours**. The Buyer must not be required to incur cost or give guarantees.
  - Include a sunset date and a Buyer walk right.
  - Consider a warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received. Also consider a price adjustment or earn-out holdback if Bluefen terminates within, say, 12 months for change-of-control reasons.

### 9. Riverlark facility of about AUD 3.2m (cl 2 / 7) — HIGH
- **Facts (DL 3):** The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security has been provided. It contains change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.
- **Issue:** A "release to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. If the release does not arrive, Riverlark's security over the Company's assets (and possibly over the shares) survives, and Completion could itself trigger an event of default under clause 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion, require:
    - a **payout letter**; and
    - an executed **deed of release** under clause 9.2, covering all security, PPSR registrations and any guarantees from the Company.
  - Repayment should come out of the purchase price through the funds flow, paid directly to Riverlark, with PPSR discharges effected at Completion or held in escrow with the Buyer's lawyers.
  - The amount should be included in **Debt**, deducted from the price.
  - Confirm whether Riverlark holds a mortgage over the shares. If it does, this goes to title (see item 15).

### 10. DD-005 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 plus on-costs — HIGH (price leakage)
- **Facts (DL 5):** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. They are **not in the funds flow**, and the letter is silent on on-costs.
- **Issue:** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but does not fund them. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer effectively pays AUD 420,000 plus:
  - NSW payroll tax (currently about 5.45%, subject to threshold);
  - superannuation guarantee, if the bonuses are ordinary time earnings (to be confirmed);
  - PAYG withholding administration; and
  - workers' compensation premiums.
  
  The total exposure is roughly AUD 445k–500k.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses and all on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt**, deducted from the price. Alternatively, the Seller funds them at Completion through the funds flow, with payment processed through Company payroll.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall and any post-Completion bonus claims.
  - If the deal uses a locked box, these are **leakage**.
  - Confirm the documents give no Buyer-side retention obligation.

### 11. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1) — HIGH
- **Facts (DL 4):** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 outstanding. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Issue:** On those facts, the Company **may not own** the SOW3 IP. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment. It does not cover:
  - the Company not owning the IP;
  - third-party infringement claims;
  - the cost of re-engineering; or
  - lost revenue if the materials are used in core products.
- **Push back:**
  - Completion deliverables:
    - evidence of cleared payment, or payment out of the price through the funds flow; and
    - an executed **confirmatory assignment** from Ironquay of all SOW3 IP, including moral rights consents where relevant.
  - A specific IP indemnity covering all loss from any failure of title to the SOW3 materials. It should not be subject to the general cap, thresholds or disclosure, should last at least 6 years, and should be capped at the price or at an agreed figure supported by technical due diligence.
  - Have the technical team confirm how central the SOW3 materials are to the product.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6) — HIGH, unquantified
- **Facts (DL 6):** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may expose about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notifiability are unknown, and the investigation is still "preliminary."
- **Issue:** The Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material," but the disclosure itself establishes nothing either way.
  - Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment within 30 days. The letter is dated as at 22 September 2026 and today is 6 November 2026, so that window has very likely closed. A missed assessment or notification may be a separate contravention.
  - Exposure includes OAIC investigation, the increased civil penalties, the statutory privacy tort, customer contract claims (check whether Bluefen's contract has data or security clauses), and remediation costs.
- **Push back:**
  - Before signing or as a CP, require the full incident file: forensic report, access logs, the Company's NDB assessment and any notifications made.
  - Pre-Completion covenant that the Seller completes the investigation and makes any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer.
  - **Specific indemnity** for all loss arising from DD-006, including regulatory fines to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, third-party claims and remediation. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, last at least 3–4 years, and be backed by escrow.
  - Add an express warranty on compliance with the Privacy Act and data incidents. Confirm whether W&I insurers will exclude this as a known matter. They almost certainly will, which is why the indemnity matters.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals of AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts (DL 8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The letter says they should be "read together for timing/scope" and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Issue:** The Seller calls these "ordinary course," but the letter does not support that. Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three may have been done to stay under a materiality or Buyer-consent threshold in the conduct-of-business covenant or the material contracts definition. I can't confirm this without the full SPA thresholds. Please check.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain the contracts and confirm timing (before or after signing), term, termination rights, and whether they are related-party arrangements.
  - Add an aggregation rule: related contracts count together for all thresholds.
  - If entered after the relevant date without consent or outside the ordinary course, treat them as leakage or a Debt-like item, or require the Seller to procure termination.
  - Ensure any amount accrued or prepaid is properly reflected in working capital.

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Push back:** Reject.
  - **Tax:** A separate **tax indemnity / covenant** covering pre-Completion tax, capped at 100% of the price, running for the ATO amendment period plus a buffer. No disclosure against it and no de minimis or basket.
  - **IP:** IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement, assignments from employees and contractors, and open-source use. Put them at a higher cap, or treat key IP ownership as quasi-fundamental, given the Ironquay facts.

### 15. Title (DD-012)
- **Issue:** The Company's share register is the Seller's own record. DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Push back:**
  - Run ASIC company searches (members and share structure) and PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company. Also review constitution and shareholder documents for options, convertible notes, ESOP or pre-emption rights.
  - The title warranty must cover full legal and beneficial ownership free of all Encumbrances, with no options or rights to issue shares. Treat it as fundamental (see item 4).
  - Completion deliverables: share transfer, share certificates (or an indemnity for lost certificates), and releases of any share security, including possibly Riverlark's.

### 16. Lower-risk items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation only. Add a covenant that the Seller procures the notice is given on time, and confirm the lease contains no change-of-control termination right.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Confirm the clause contains no "deemed assignment on change of control" wording. If it does, treat it like Bluefen.

## Part D: Structural protections

- **Escrow or retention:** Hold back about 10–15% of the price (AUD 2.4m–3.6m) for 18–24 months to secure the specific indemnities. DD-006 is the priority because it is unquantified. Alternatively, require a creditworthy guarantee, because Harbourglass may distribute the proceeds.
- **W&I insurance:** Worth considering for general warranties. Known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar) will be excluded, so they must be covered by Seller indemnities or price.
- **Funds flow:** Reissue it to show Riverlark payout, the bonuses and on-costs, Ironquay payment (if made from the price) and Transaction Costs as deductions. Confirm whether the deal uses **completion accounts or a locked box**, because this affects how items 10 and 13 are treated.
- **Conduct of business:** Pre-Completion covenants should require Buyer consent for new or renewed contracts above a threshold, measured on an aggregated basis, for bonuses, and for any communications with regulators about DD-006.
